note: RECOMMENDED CREATIVE STYLE per concept (TOF bank v2, 40 concepts). Each tile maps to one of 12 on-brand StoreHub style archetypes shown as a photoreal mockup; drawer gives build direction. Rebuilt 2026-07-01.

PAIN-01.why: A busy café closes and the whole night's takings sit as a snowdrift of order chits on the floor, nothing actually logged. One night of trading, and not a number you can trust.
PAIN-01.steal: Upmarket café after close in warm evening light, floor blanketed in a snowdrift of order chits, a well-dressed Pan-Asian owner standing marooned in the middle with a phone in hand, clean modern fit-out behind.

PAIN-02.why: A boutique goes dark in the middle of a busy shopping afternoon because the owner is stuck reconciling yesterday, and every shopper who finds the door shut simply walks next door.
PAIN-02.steal: Bright upmarket boutique on a busy 2pm shopping street, blinds down and a bold card in the glass door reading 'CLOSED — DOING YESTERDAY'S BOOKS', well-dressed Pan-Asian shoppers drifting to the store next door.

PAIN-03.why: The kitchen is winning but the payment line is losing: a queue snakes out the door and round the block, and diners peel away before they ever pay.
PAIN-03.steal: Bird's-eye of a stylish full-service restaurant at peak, a payment queue snaking out the door and round the block, three well-dressed Pan-Asian diners peeling away tagged 'GONE', warm daylight, clean modern fit-out.

PAIN-05.why: A wall of handwritten kitchen chits turns one scribbled 'no onions' into a wrong plate on the pass, and a good table turns into an angry one.
PAIN-05.steal: Modern open-kitchen bistro pass, a wall papered with handwritten kitchen chits, one ringed in orange reading 'Table 12 — NO onions', a wrong plate sitting under the heat lamp, a Pan-Asian chef mid-service, clean upmarket fit-out.

NEW-01.why: A sleek new cafe wears a giant orange '02' in the window as the owner calmly flips the sign to OPEN. The whole setup of outlet one cloned to outlet two in an afternoon, both on one dashboard.
NEW-01.steal: A sleek newly-fitted cafe at golden hour, a giant orange '02' decal filling the front window, a calm confident Pan-Asian owner flipping the sign to OPEN, clean modern interior behind.

NEW-03.why: A freshly framed business-registration certificate hangs on a clean wall, a phone beside it reading 'e-Invoice: compliant.' A brand-new business, compliant from day one because e-Invoice is built in.
NEW-03.steal: A framed fresh business-registration certificate on a clean white wall of a tasteful new cafe, a phone propped beside it showing 'e-Invoice: compliant', soft natural light, no brand chrome up top.

NEW-04.why: A grand-opening queue stretches down a bright street under an 'OUTLET 2' banner while the owner calmly rings the first order on a handheld and a diner scans a QR tent. QR clears the opening rush and the setup cloned before the doors opened.
NEW-04.steal: A grand-opening queue stretching down a bright modern high street outside a stylish new cafe, an 'OUTLET 2' banner overhead, a composed Pan-Asian owner taking the first order on a handheld while a diner scans a QR table tent, energetic upmarket vibe.

QUIET-02.why: A torn order-pad page with one biro line sits on clean marble, a faded receipt half in the bin. The shoebox of loose paper is gone, because every sale now files itself, compliant.
QUIET-02.steal: Overhead on cool marble, a single torn order-pad page with one fading biro line, a faded receipt half-dropped into a bin at the edge of frame, and bold orange type across the negative space reading 'SHOEBOX, RETIRED.' Minimal, upmarket, Pan-Asian SEA cafe.

QUIET-03.why: At 6pm an understated owner locks a tidy upmarket boutique in golden light; the phone reads 'Today's report: ready. Sent to your inbox.' The reports wrote themselves and can be checked from anywhere.
QUIET-03.steal: Golden-hour exterior of a tidy, upmarket boutique, a calm Pan-Asian SEA owner turning the key on a clean glass door, phone in hand showing a StoreHub-styled line: 'Today's report: ready. Sent to your inbox.' Warm, aspirational, unhurried.

MATH-01.why: A cafe wall is tiled floor to ceiling with 365 teh tarik glasses, one glass for every day of the year. A hand lifts one and a price stamp fills the empty slot: a single daily glass buys a whole year of running your shop.
MATH-01.steal: A bright, well-fitted specialty cafe with a feature wall tiled floor-to-ceiling in 365 clean teh tarik glasses catching warm window light; a Pan-Asian SEA owner in a crisp apron lifts one glass as a sharp orange price card fills the empty slot.

MATH-02.why: A year wall-calendar hangs behind a tired owner; 30 evenings are stamped 'COUNTING' and bleed down into a pile of receipts at her feet. That is a whole month of nights lost every year to counting up by hand.
MATH-02.steal: A calm, upmarket bistro after close in warm low light, a large tasteful year-calendar on a clean feature wall with 30 evenings marked; a poised Pan-Asian SEA owner stands beside it with a neat stack of receipts on the counter.

MATH-03.why: An airport split-flap board on a bistro wall clacks through the digits and settles on 'TODAY: RM8,420 . RECONCILED' while the owner just sips a coffee beneath it. The day added itself up; nobody sat down to count.
MATH-03.steal: A stylish full-service bistro at golden hour with an eye-catching airport split-flap board on the clean brick feature wall; a relaxed Pan-Asian SEA owner sits beneath it with a flat white, unhurried and successful.

MATH-04.why: A giant orange '48' crashes down mid-air into a black '0' above a bare boutique shelf. The system swears you have 48 in stock; the shelf has none. Ghost stock just cost you the sale.
MATH-04.steal: A bright, well-fitted fashion boutique with clean minimalist shelving, one shelf conspicuously empty under sculptural oversized orange '48' and black '0' numerals floating mid-air; a Pan-Asian SEA shopper reaches for a shelf that is bare, upmarket fit-out throughout.

CON-01.why: A split set: on the left, a cluttered legacy counter buried in add-on boxes and cables; on the right, the same counter clean with a single slim terminal. The owner is caught mid-step toward the right, one screen instead of the whole tangle.
CON-01.steal: A stylish boutique-cafe counter shown as a clean before/after split; the rejected left side is a cramped legacy setup with tangled cables and stacked add-on boxes, the aspirational right side is a bright, minimal upmarket counter with one slim StoreHub terminal; a Pan-Asian SEA owner steps confidently to the right.

CON-02.why: A polished brass balance scale sits perfectly level: on one pan a glass of teh tarik, on the other a slim POS terminal. They weigh exactly the same, your whole system costs what your daily drink costs.
CON-02.steal: A warm, upmarket cafe tabletop in soft daylight with an elegant brass balance scale sitting level, a glass of teh tarik on one pan and a slim StoreHub terminal on the other; clean marble surface, tasteful and aspirational, Pan-Asian SEA hands steadying the scale.

CON-03.why: A sleek museum vitrine stands in a bright modern boutique; the brass plaque reads 'MANUAL CASH REGISTER, c. NOW', with a paper spike, a cash drawer and a ledger displayed inside like fossils. A shopper squints, people still run their shop on this?
CON-03.steal: A bright, upmarket concept boutique with polished floors and gallery lighting, one glass museum vitrine on a plinth displaying a paper spike, cash drawer and ledger behind a 'c. NOW' plaque; a stylish Pan-Asian SEA shopper leans in, amused, while the surrounding shop is modern and aspirational and the old props stay only inside the case.

CON-04.why: A shredder eats a fistful of crumpled handwritten receipts, but what slides out the other side is not confetti, it is a phone showing a clean, compliant e-Invoice. Paper in, compliant out.
CON-04.steal: A crisp, modern cafe back-office corner with a clean desk in good light; a Pan-Asian SEA owner feeds a shoebox of old handwritten receipts into a sleek shredder while a phone at the output end shows a tidy StoreHub e-Invoice, the paper receipts being the rejected before and the phone the aspirational now.

PROOF-01.why: A night map of Southeast Asia glows with 20,000+ tiny orange shop-lights, and one flares brighter, the seat that's still open.
PROOF-01.steal: A cinematic night-time map of Southeast Asia rendered in deep brand black, dotted with 20,000+ tiny warm-orange shop-lights, one light pulsing brighter than the rest.

PROOF-03.why: A giant orange '20,000+' is built entirely from thousands of real storefront photo tiles; pull back and the number resolves.
PROOF-03.steal: A giant brand-orange '20,000+' composed of thousands of real Pan-Asian SEA storefront photo tiles, modern cafés, bistros and boutiques, resolving into one bold number as the camera pulls back.

CULTURE-02.why: A single unbroken tracking shot glides down a Ramadan bazaar lane and lands on one polished premium stall where diners tap to pay while the queue never stops moving.
CULTURE-02.steal: A vibrant Ramadan bazaar lane at dusk shot as one unbroken glide, retuned to warm brand-orange lanterns and pelita, landing on a single upmarket, beautifully-lit food stall with a clean modern fit-out where Pan-Asian SEA diners tap-to-pay on a slim terminal while the line keeps flowing.

CULTURE-03.why: The instant buka puasa begins, a packed modern bistro rings in a wall of orders at once and a giant stamp reads '214 orders. 90 seconds.' Every one landed live.
CULTURE-03.steal: A packed, stylish full-service bistro at the precise second of buka puasa, warm brand-orange pelita and ketupat decor (retuned orange, never green), Pan-Asian SEA diners breaking fast together as staff calmly ring every order into a slim POS.

CULTURE-04.why: A Deepavali boutique surges in orange motion-streaks while dead-centre, in razor focus, one calm POS shows live stock that never lets a box oversell.
CULTURE-04.steal: An upmarket Deepavali sweets-and-sari boutique at full festive surge, Pan-Asian SEA shoppers blurred into warm brand-orange motion-streaks (never green), clean modern fit-out and rich lighting, with one calm slim POS in razor focus at centre showing live stock counts.

CULTURE-06.why: A floor-to-ceiling wall of Mid-Autumn mooncake gift boxes; a merchant taps one pre-order and a stamp reads '2,000 boxes. 0 oversold.'
CULTURE-06.steal: An elegant, well-lit Mid-Autumn boutique with a floor-to-ceiling wall of premium mooncake gift boxes glowing under warm brand-orange lantern light (never green), a Pan-Asian SEA merchant calmly tapping a pre-order into a slim POS.

SELF-02.why: One owner has cut ten ribbons at ten upmarket outlets, and an eleventh frame waits empty with the ribbon still in hand. Every outlet runs off a single login, one source of truth.
SELF-02.steal: A gallery wall in a stylish flagship cafe office, ten framed ribbon-cutting photos of the same confident Pan-Asian owner at ten upmarket outlets, an eleventh frame empty with a fresh ribbon in hand, warm modern lighting.

SELF-03.why: A hand hefts a heavy keyring of five outlet keys, the fifth still shiny and new. Five outlets, one dashboard, the same live numbers wherever the owner is.
SELF-03.steal: Overhead close-up of a confident owner's hand holding a heavy brass-and-orange keyring on a marble counter in an upmarket boutique, five keys tagged 01 to 05 with the fifth visibly shiny and new, clean modern fit-out.

SELF-04.why: The same upmarket cafe storefront repeats identically into the distance like a hall of mirrors. Set the standard once and it pushes to every outlet, so no two ever drift apart.
SELF-04.steal: A serene hall-of-mirrors effect where the same warmly-lit upmarket cafe storefront repeats identically into the distance, clean fit-out, calm confident Pan-Asian staff at each, soft golden light.

SELF-05.why: A bold card fills the glass door of a busy upmarket shop: 'OWNER'S OFF TODAY. SHOP ISN'T.' Service hums with no owner in sight, because every sale logs itself and every outlet stays in sync from anywhere.
SELF-05.steal: Through the glass door of a busy upmarket boutique-cafe, a large clean typographic card is the hero reading 'OWNER'S OFF TODAY. SHOP ISN'T' while polished Pan-Asian staff serve a full room behind it, warm modern lighting, no owner in sight.

HC-01.why: A small daily leak feels like nothing, until a fare-meter on the counter climbs to RM4,380 and shows you what a year of tiny untracked losses really costs.
HC-01.steal: A photoreal fare-meter sitting on a polished café counter, orange digits ticking up toward RM4,380, a soft caption 'small daily leaks — this year', warm upmarket café interior behind, a Pan-Asian owner watching quietly.

HC-02.why: A grid of 52 boxes shows every Sunday of the year, all but one greyed out because they were spent on paperwork instead of rest, and it adds up to a full day off every single week.
HC-02.steal: A clean grid of 52 takeaway boxes on a bright studio-lit surface, 51 grey and one glowing orange and empty, caption 'Sundays you spent on paperwork — 52 / year', modern upmarket styling, no clutter.

HC-03.why: An x-ray sweep across a pristine boutique shelf shows half the products as translucent ghosts, revealing that the system says 48 while the shelf actually holds 19.
HC-03.steal: Pristine upmarket boutique shelf under clean gallery lighting, an x-ray overlay revealing half the products as translucent ghosts, caption 'System says 48. Shelf has 19.', a Pan-Asian retail owner studying the shelf.

HC-04.why: A split frame joined by an equals sign puts a café that is full every night against a bank balance sitting at zero, asking where all that busy actually goes.
HC-04.steal: A black split frame divided by a bold equals sign, the left side a heaving upmarket café captioned 'Full every night', the right side a flat bank balance reading 'RM0 left', clean high-contrast graphic styling, Pan-Asian diners on the left.

VALUE-01.why: The cafe closes at dusk, apron on the hook, and the owner is already gone home. Because the day's takings reconciled themselves live as each order rang, closing is done before the lights go off.
VALUE-01.steal: A warm, well-fitted cafe at dusk, a large orange wall clock reading 6:03, an apron hung neatly on its hook, chairs stacked, and through the front window a family dinner glowing in a home across the street; the Pan-Asian SEA owner is already walking out, calm.

VALUE-02.why: Midnight in a tidy back office: one chair pulled out from a receipt-piled desk sits empty under a desk lamp. Nobody came to count tonight, because every order already logged itself.
VALUE-02.steal: A tidy back office of an upmarket restaurant at midnight, a single desk lamp pooling light over an empty chair pulled out from a desk still stacked with the day's receipts, untouched; a small stamped card reads 'not tonight.' Warm, cinematic, Pan-Asian SEA.

VALUE-03.why: A slim tablet stands alone on a clean boutique counter beside a toppled heap of the eight tools it made obsolete. One screen now does the work of all of them.
VALUE-03.steal: A bright, established boutique counter, spotless, with a single slim StoreHub tablet standing upright beside a neatly toppled heap of eight retired tools (old terminal, receipt books, stock binder, loyalty stamp cards, invoice folders) pushed to the discard side; clean modern retail, Pan-Asian SEA staff.

ARTIFACT-01.why: A phone lock-screen with no brand chrome floods with StoreHub-styled 'New order received' pings at the dinner peak, stacking faster than you can read, then a calm reveal: every order was captured the second it landed.
ARTIFACT-01.steal: A close, phone-in-hand shot of a clean lock-screen (no brand chrome, StoreHub-styled generic-neutral notifications) inside a warm, busy upmarket café at dinner peak, 'New order received' pings cascading and stacking faster than they can be read.

ARTIFACT-02.why: A proud merchant screenshots their StoreHub sales summary like a personal-best post — 'Today: 347 orders · RM18,240 · busiest hour 8-9pm.' The numbers were live and ready the moment they wanted to share.
ARTIFACT-02.steal: Close on a phone held over a warm modern bistro pass, the screen showing a clean StoreHub-styled sales-summary card in orange and black reading 'Today: 347 orders · RM18,240 · busiest hour 8-9pm', caught mid-screenshot; no ad chrome, it reads like the owner's own proud post. Pan-Asian SEA hand.

ARTIFACT-04.why: A StoreHub-styled confirmation slip sits on a cafe counter — 'e-Invoice submitted ✓ · 1,204 invoices · this month.' Every invoice filed itself as each sale rang, with nothing left to submit.
ARTIFACT-04.steal: Overhead on a clean marble cafe counter, a single StoreHub-styled confirmation slip (orange tick, black text: 'e-Invoice submitted ✓ · 1,204 invoices · this month') resting beside a flat white coffee; no ad chrome, it looks like a real merchant's counter. Warm, upmarket, Pan-Asian SEA.

ARTIFACT-05.why: A single order-ticket ribbon unfurls from a café pass and pools across the floor; a stamp reads 'One festival night. All of it, logged.' The reveal: nobody counted it, it counted itself.
ARTIFACT-05.steal: An upmarket café pass at the close of a busy night, a single continuous order-ticket ribbon unfurling and pooling elegantly across a clean tiled floor under warm brand-orange light, no staff hunched over counting.

MILE-01.why: A restaurant facade blazes with a giant orange light-bulb marquee reading RM1,000,000 as the owner and staff cheer on the street. The milestone lands with nothing to reconcile because every ringgit was tracked and compliant from day one.
MILE-01.steal: A handsome full-service restaurant facade wrapped in a giant orange light-bulb marquee reading 'RM1,000,000', the owner and polished Pan-Asian staff cheering out on the bright street at dusk, celebratory and upmarket.

MILE-03.why: A freshly opened boutique with the ribbon still on the door and a giant orange 'DAY 1' in the window; a small line reads 'e-Invoice: ✓ already compliant.' Brand-new, and already sorted.
MILE-03.steal: A bright, freshly-opened boutique storefront, a cut ribbon still draped on the glass door, a giant orange 'DAY 1' decal filling the window, a small line beneath reading 'e-Invoice: ✓ already compliant.' Beaming Pan-Asian SEA owner, clean modern fit-out.
